body:
[A10] Found by the #397 service-budget reviews (PR #588: R349-1 F1, issuecomment-5855813802; R348-1 F1, issuecomment-5855875344). This is a product defect on the shipping 1x1.

## Observed

- The firmware's NVM writer heartbeat comes only from `nvm_heartbeat_tick()` (`sw/firmware/milan_baremetal/milan_baremetal.c:757-769`, rate-limited to 250 ms). It is called from the idle hook (`:1115-1120`) and from the flash, restore and device poll loops. No console handler calls it (`:1516-1584`).
- The BIOS runs the idle hook only while no UART byte is pending (LiteX `readline.c`: `while (!uart_read_nonblock()) idle_hook_ptr();`). The UART RX ring is 128 bytes.
- Queued console input therefore suppresses every heartbeat between commands. Reviewer probe P3 ran the **unmodified** firmware on the product-CPU simulation (1x1), with a 133-byte pasted plan (`milan_nvm` x12, then `milan_status`):
  - one heartbeat was written, at 252.6 ms;
  - `backed=1` held through a status read at ≤1,936 ms after it;
  - `backed=0` appeared from ≤2,145 ms. The T-NVM-WRITER-ALIVE of 2,000 ms (`docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md` §9.4) lapsed.
- On the 8x8, a single `milan_nvm` status command runs 788.9 ms with no heartbeat opportunity, against the 500 ms heartbeat period.

## Decision (manager)

Queued console input is in scope. An operator pasting commands must never lapse the saved-state liveness. The fix belongs in the firmware's service structure, under #397's option (a): one hart, with the rule that no duty may run past the smallest deadline without a tick opportunity. A second hart is not the remedy for this defect.

## Acceptance

1. A heartbeat tick opportunity at each console command dispatch, and inside every console handler or walk that can exceed the tick period (including the 8x8 `nvm status` path). The existing 250 ms rate limit is unchanged.
2. On the product-CPU simulation, both shapes:
   - P3-style queued input (≥133 bytes, back-to-back commands) keeps `backed=1` for the whole run;
   - the longest no-tick stretch of every duty stays below 500 ms minus the rate-limit phase;
   - a committed control fails when the dispatch tick is removed.
3. **Firmware change, so the capture gate applies:** re-measure the capture per `tb/verilator/nvm_capture_cpu/README.md` (#559 procedure). STOP if the 8x8 exceeds 24.5 ms.
4. Record the change in `docs/integration/BAREMETAL_FIRMWARE.md`, including the single-long-command and chained-short-command cases.

ALINX focus. Depends on #397's measurement harness (PR #588).

comments.body: [A10] Paired with #592, the word-wide capture copy. Both firmware changes land in one lane with one capture re-measure. The lane starts after PR #588 (the #397 measurement harness) merges, because this issue's acceptance probes use it.

[A10] ASSIGNMENT: one firmware lane for #590, #592 and #599, with one capture re-measure. Executor [A385]; reviewers [R368] (internal) and [R369] (external). Branch `590-592-599-firmware` from dev `8bc97021`, which includes PR #588's #397 measurement harness.

**Scope:**
1. **#590:** acceptance 1-4 as written, plus the #397 findings-page refresh listed on #590 (5857603294). A heartbeat tick opportunity goes at each console dispatch and inside every handler or walk that can exceed the tick period. The 250 ms rate limit is unchanged.
2. **#592:** acceptance 1-4 as written. Word-wide loads and stores inside each record; the byte path only for edges; byte-identical snapshots; a planted byte-only control restores the old timing.
3. **#599:** acceptance 1, 2, 3 and 5.
   - The firmware polls PHY link, speed and duplex over the existing bit-bang MDIO window and writes `link_status`. No new fabric MDIO master.
   - The poll period is derived from the #397 service budget and stated, never mirrored. It fits the one-hart rule: no duty runs past the smallest deadline without a tick opportunity, and the heartbeat stays ≤ 500 ms.
   - A host or firmware test, plus a simulation check, show one LINK_DOWN and one LINK_UP per link cycle and MAC_STATUS updating. A mutant that stops the publish is killed.
   - #599 acceptance 4 (the bench re-run) is a separate lane after merge.
4. **One capture re-measure** per `tb/verilator/nvm_capture_cpu/README.md` (#559 procedure), after all three changes: both shapes, traffic ON and OFF, 16 captures each, plus the labelled 100 MHz 8x8 point. Record the processor pin and the firmware digest the receipt binds. **STOP** if the 8x8 exceeds 24.5 ms.
5. **#397 harness re-run** at the final head: every duty's worst no-tick stretch on both shapes, against the budget.

**Decisions:**
- Tick placement: where the time can be long, not everywhere. Each placement is justified by a measured stretch.
- The MDIO poll must not starve the console or the NVM writer. If one MDIO transaction plus the poll bookkeeping would exceed any budget term, STOP and report the numbers.

**Not in scope:** RTL, the builder, the processor, configurations, and the #587/#229 area work. The Arty configurations must keep building (#583). Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

**Gates** (all rc 0):
- the full builder bank in both compiler modes;
- `sw/firmware/nvm_hosttest/test_nvm_firmware.py --self-test` (every shape, Arty included);
- the firmware census gate;
- `check_nvm_capture.py` with the new receipt;
- the #397 harness;
- `scripts/ci_scope.py --selftest`;
- the docs gates;
- `git diff --check`.

[A385] TAKEN
Branch: 590-592-599-firmware at 8bc97021f28fb7f729418d3a00851c84ea0b50fd.
Authoritative references: #590, #592, #599 and the assignment above; #397 and PR #588; BAREMETAL_FIRMWARE.md; SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md section 9.4; REGISTER_MAP.md.
Interpreted scope: console heartbeat opportunities, word-wide capture copy and firmware MDIO link publication in one lane. The #599 bench rerun follows after merge. Internal reviewer [R368]; external reviewer [R369].
Validation plan: full builder bank in both compiler modes, every-shape firmware host self-test, firmware census, one final capture re-measure and receipt gate, service-budget harness, CI scope self-test, docs gates and git diff --check. Observe the assignment's capture and MDIO STOP conditions.
Blockers: none identified during assignment read.

[A385] STOP

Head: `8bc97021f28fb7f729418d3a00851c84ea0b50fd` (unchanged; the implementation is an uncommitted working draft).

The firmware census is blocked by a scope conflict. In both compiler modes, `sw/builder/test_builder.py:13304` asserts exactly two selections for its planted conditional. The optional MDIO implementation introduces a second conditional group, so the fixture now correctly enumerates four selections and fails that fixed-count assertion. The assignment excludes builder edits, so that file remains unchanged. A correction to this test fixture needs an explicit scope decision before this gate can be cleared; no assertion has been removed or weakened.

Reproduction entry points from the candidate workspace with its existing Python dependencies and compiler selector (both runs exited 1 at that assertion):

```sh
rtk proxy timeout 1800 python3 -B -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"sw/builder"); import test_builder; test_builder.test_baremetal_profile_contract()'
rtk proxy timeout 1800 python3 -B sw/builder/test_firmware_compiler.py --absent --audit /tmp/a385-census-absent.jsonl
```

The compiler-present run selected RV32 GCC 14.3.0. It passed the baseline contract check before reaching the fixture assertion. The absent run explicitly skipped the compiler-dependent instruments and failed the same fixture assertion; it is not compiled-census evidence.

Preliminary checks: the existing firmware host self-test passes all five shapes including Arty and kills all four existing mutants. The new PHY host test passes and kills a missing-publication mutant. Service-harness self-tests and the CI-scope self-test pass. The foreground 8x8 / 50 MHz / traffic-on capture arm completed with rc 0: 16/16 captures, minimum 13.21794 ms, maximum 13.23262 ms against the 24.5 ms bar, zero mismatches and zero open-record copies. All captures had concurrent requests, responses and reads. Processor pin: `870ff88ad35bbd532244e4c7e6d7661b9f6e1366`. This is preliminary draft evidence, not the required complete re-measure or final-head gate set.

The required final-head service measurements, MDIO target timing and fabric-link simulation, remaining capture arms and receipt replacement, timing/dispatch controls, documentation updates and full builder banks are incomplete. No commit or REVIEW READY claim is offered. No push, PR operation, merge, hardware, RTL, processor, configuration or builder change was made.

The working draft, proposed unapplied fixture adjustment, command logs, artifact hashes, HANDOFF.md and draft PR-BODY.md are retained in the assigned output directory. Firmware SHA-256: `c4ae162d591beb89c44cb1092a6b93134df99fc1d6997271cbe877ee181b574c`.

[A10] Scope correction and sequencing for [A385]'s STOP (firmware lane #590/#592/#599).

1. **Builder fixture edit authorized, limited to what the firmware forces.** In `sw/builder/test_builder.py:13304`, the planted-conditional selection count follows the new conditional MDIO group (2 becomes 4), per the proposed fixture patch or an equivalent. It enumerates the real selections; it does not remove or weaken an assertion. No other builder change. Then run the full builder bank in both compiler modes.
2. **Sequencing: the final capture re-measure runs on the tree that merges.**
   - PR #591 (#580) is next in the merge train. It moves the processor pin to `16be6768` and records its own capture receipt at that pin.
   - So this lane resumes after #580 merges. First, commit the working draft as the per-issue commits. Then `git merge origin/dev` (merge commit, resolution only). Then finish the remaining items at the merged head: the service measurements, the MDIO timing and the fabric-link simulation, all capture arms with the receipt replaced and its processor pin describing the measured tree, the controls, the docs, and every gate.
   - The preliminary 8x8 result (13.23 ms at pin `870ff88a`) is recorded as preliminary only.

The lane's worktree keeps the uncommitted draft; nothing else touches it until the resume.

title: Queued console input starves the NVM writer heartbeat and lapses liveness
